title: Finite-power coordinates after scalar restriction detect preservation of finite limits
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the coefficient universe, with abelian sheafification whose local equivalences are monoidal, and give $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,\operatorname{Ab})$ the sheafified tensor product of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $\varphi:R\to B$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] of $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,\operatorname{Ab})$. Write $\operatorname{Mod}_R$ and $\operatorname{Mod}_B$ for their categories of internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:\operatorname{Mod}_B\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ for restriction of scalars [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. For an integer $n\geq0$, let $P_n:\operatorname{Mod}_R\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ send $M$ to the product $M^n$ of $n$ copies, with componentwise action, and send $f$ to $f^n$; set $M^0=0$. If a functor $T:\operatorname{Mod}_R\to\operatorname{Mod}_B$ is equipped with a natural isomorphism $\alpha:\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\circ T\xrightarrow{\sim}P_n$, then $T$ preserves finite limits. Explicitly, for every finite category $J$ and diagram $D:J\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ with limit cone $(L,(p_j)_j)$, the cone $(T(L),(T(p_j))_j)$ is a limit cone in $\operatorname{Mod}_B$, including when $J$ is empty.

proof.text: The canonical sheaf tensor is closed by sfbSheafTensor_properties and is therefore monoidally preadditive by sfbSheafTensor_monoidalPreadditive. This proves the infrastructure conjunct. For the remaining conjunct use the arbitrary MonoidalPreadditive instance in its universal quantifier.

Use the existing internal-module limit construction [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-creates], realized by CategoryTheory.Mod.createsLimit in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Mod.Limits. For any monoid A the forgetful functor U_A creates limits, hence preserves and reflects finite limits. The abelian category of sheaves has finite limits, so the internal module categories have finite limits and their finite powers exist. No sectionwise equivalence or restriction-reflection argument is needed.

The constant-diagram functor preserves limits by Mathlib CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesLimits_const, and the limit functor preserves limits by CategoryTheory.Limits.lim_preservesLimits (it is right adjoint to the constant-diagram functor). Thus P_n = Functor.const (Discrete (Fin n)) followed by lim preserves finite limits. This includes n = 0 and empty limit diagrams. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-exactness-nat-iso] to alpha inverse to obtain preservation by T followed by scalar restriction.

By the definition of restriction [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], Res_phi followed by U_R is definitionally U_B, on both objects and maps. Composing preservation of T followed by Res_phi with preservation by U_R gives preservation by T followed by U_B. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-limit-preservation-cancellation] with F=T and V=U_B, whose reflection of finite limits was supplied by the creation result. Hence T preserves finite limits.
